scenes.heading: Pricing beyond the shoot: prints, albums, licensing

sents.d: Pricing beyond the shoot: prints, albums, licensing
The shoot fee is often the smallest part of potential revenue.
Many photographers price only for the time spent shooting and editing, leaving significant revenue on the table.
Prints, albums, wall art, and licensing for commercial use can often generate more than the original session fee.

scenes.heading: Bring up prints and albums early

sents.d: Build these into your pricing conversation from the start rather than as an afterthought — for example, offering a session fee that includes a small print credit, with albums and larger prints priced separately.
For commercial or brand photography specifically, always clarify usage rights and charge more for exclusive or extended-use licensing versus one-time use.

take: Price prints, albums and licensing into the first conversation.
